events.text: Opaque grid made the lines VANISH — they're sub-pixel-thin (0.006-0.012m) and were only visible via the transparent blend's coverage; opaque they rasterize to nothing. Reverted to translucent (grid visible again). Pivoted the skip fix to the actual remaining lever: host camera smoothing. Default is now cameraSmoothing=0 (DIRECT 1:1 tracking, like Blockbench — no 42ms momentum/lag), applied via ctl.setSmoothing on mount, plus a live 'smooth:' button (bottom-right) cycling direct/24/80/160 so the feel can be dialed against Blockbench. Hot-reload, fps untouched.

resolution: The probe ruled out every framerate cause: [studio-cam-host] shows camHz=240 / avgDt=4.17ms / camSteps/s=240 (camera advances EVERY render frame, not at a slow tick), fps=240 solid, 0 skips, gc=0 (0 fired, genuinely never runs). And the user's Blockbench clue (direct camera at 112fps feels smooth, ours skips at 240fps) means it is NOT a fps problem. The smoking gun is in the r3d-census: tcount=26 — the 26 ground-grid lines are TRANSLUCENT (opacity 0.85), so they ride the back-to-front transparent pipeline and get re-sorted every frame; as the camera orbits, their sort order flips at angles and they pop/flicker, which reads as the scene 'skipping' during a spin (independent of the smooth 240Hz camera, and exactly what Blockbench's grid does not do). Fix: the grid lines are now OPAQUE (material is a color string like the origin axes already are), so they join the depth-tested opaque pass with no per-frame sort. Single-variable change so the result is interpretable — verify in the next census that tcount goes 26->0 and mcount 3->29, and the spin should stop popping. If a residual skip remains, the next lever is the camera smoothing (24/s ≈ 42ms lag) which I'll expose as a live control. Hot-reload TSX, fps untouched.
